source_reachability:
I re-fetched every URL myself with curl -A "Mokaair-editorial" and inspected the BODY, not just the status code.

- https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/08/21/2026-17183.txt — HTTP 200, 795,262 bytes, 13,701 lines, genuine FR full text (HTML-wrapped <pre>; header "Federal Register Volume 91, Number 161 (Friday, August 21, 2026)", "[FR Doc No: 2026-17183]").
- https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-21/pdf/2026-17183.pdf — HTTP 200, 5,538,351 bytes, valid PDF 1.7; pypdf reports 146 pages; page 1 header "54510 Federal Register / Vol. 91, No. 161 / Friday, August 21, 2026 / Proposed Rules" with SUMMARY and DATES matching the .txt verbatim. (`file` misreports "10 page(s)" from a nested /Count; there are 147 /Type/Page objects. Not a problem.)

- https://www.sec.gov/news/pressreleases.rss — HTTP 200, 18,402 bytes, 25 <item>, newest 2026-09-16 10:00 -0400. Live feed, not stale.

- https://www.sec.gov/news/statements.rss — 200, 11,975 bytes, 25 items, newest 2026-09-16.
- https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-05635.json — 200.

The researcher correctly kept it out of sources[]. This is the ONLY URL the candidate list gives for C4, so the candidate list needs fixing.

BLOCKS I RE-CONFIRMED MYSELF (all HTTP 403): www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-76-…, www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/2026/08/s7-2026-27, www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/peirce-statement-regulation-crypto-assets-081826, www.sec.gov/comments/s7-2026-27/regulation-crypto-assets, www.regulations.gov/document/SEC-2026-5190-0001, www.sec.gov/rss/rules/proposed.xml, www.sec.gov/rss/news/speeches.xml.

NO FIRST-PARTY VIOLATION FOUND: every source and every fact URL is Office of the Federal Register, GPO/GovInfo, or sec.gov. No news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet is used as a source anywhere.
NO FABRICATED IDENTIFIER FOUND: the .txt and PDF URLs are the API's own raw_text_url and pdf_url fields; press-release number 2026-76 comes from the <link> slug in the RSS; SEC-2026-5190-0001, the release numbers, RIN and CFR parts are all read off pages actually fetched.

refuted.fact: not_said: "the document never mentions the GENIUS Act (0 occurrences in the full text) and does not deal with stablecoin issuance licensing" — repeated in overlaps_existing_article as "this proposal mentions GENIUS 0 times … the two do not overlap at all, do not cross-reference them."
refuted.why: REFUTED by the source. The acronym "GENIUS" is absent, but the statute is cited by its full name in footnote 122 (.txt lines 1577-1581): "The foregoing definition of ``crypto asset'' is identical to the definition of ``Digital Asset'' in section (2)(6) of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act, Public Law 119-27, 139 Stat. 419 (July 18, 2025)." It appears at the most load-bearing point in the release: the definition that sets the proposal's entire scope. Writing "the proposal never mentions the US stablecoin act" would put a false statement in the article, and the instruction not to cross-reference C6-C9 would suppress a real, first-party-sourced connection.

refuted.fact: not_said: "'stablecoin' appears only 9 times in the full text, mostly in footnotes citing the 2025 Division of Corporation Finance staff statements."
refuted.why: REFUTED on both the count and the characterisation. My count on the fetched .txt is 10 occurrences across 9 lines (598, 616, 617×2, 676, 734, 736, 1445, 1581, 7393). Only lines 598/616/617 are the staff-statement footnote. The rest are substantive: fn 46 (Exec. Order 14178 §2(a) defines "digital asset" as including stablecoins), lines 734-736 (the 2026 Interpretation's five-category taxonomy and the view that stablecoins may or may not be securities), fn 114 line 1445 ("permitted payment stablecoins received for the covered investment contracts" count toward the aggregate offering price), fn 122 line 1581 (the GENIUS Act definitional cite). This mischaracterisation is what produced the GENIUS Act error above.

refuted.fact: F63: "This estimate is based on the number of crypto-asset-related offerings in the 2024 Regulation D, Regulation A and Regulation Crowdfunding markets (99 raising USD 5 million or less, 31 raising more than 5 million but no more than 75 million)."
refuted.why: PARTLY REFUTED. Footnote 543 (lines 10775-10781) says the 99 figure comes from "the 99 offerings involving crypto assets in the Regulation D AND Regulation Crowdfunding markets that raised $5 million or less in 2024" — Regulation A is NOT in the basis for the 99. Reg A appears only in the basis for the 31. The release explains why the baskets differ (fn 439: issuers cannot offer or sell covered investment contracts pursuant to Regulation A at all). The researcher merged the two baskets.

refuted.fact: F50 verbatim_quote: "whether the issuer has achieved decentralization would be based on how the issuer defined or otherwise described decentralization, not a general market conception of decentralization"
refuted.why: MISQUOTE. The source reads "… not a general market conception of WHAT CONSTITUTES decentralization." (footnote 193, lines 3013-3017). Two further inaccuracies in the same fact: the passage sits inside footnote 193, not in the body as "the preamble states" implies; and the supporting cite there is "2026 Interpretation at 13721", not a free-standing holding of this release. The substance is right; the quoted string must not be printed as a quotation.

unsupported.fact: editorial_brief section 3: "原始碼與白皮書要免費公開" (source code and whitepapers must be made publicly available free of charge).
unsupported.why: UNSUPPORTED, and it states a rule obligation that does not exist. Proposed Rule 103(b)(6) requires only a description of security plus, "TO THE EXTENT THE ISSUER HAS MADE IT PUBLICLY AVAILABLE, the website address at which the code … is accessible" — it does not require publishing source code at all, and says nothing about free of charge. The "publicly accessible, free of charge" wording is in Rule 103(b)(2)(v) and attaches to whitepapers and other offering materials the issuer prepared and distributed. F21 already compresses (6) to "安全性與原始碼公開網址", dropping the condition; the editorial_brief turns it into a mandate. Verified at .txt lines 12374-12384.

unsupported.fact: F70 first clause: "the full text contains 24 'Request for Comment' blocks."
unsupported.why: UNSUPPORTED. The release states no such count, so this is a researcher tally, and a straight grep gives 28 "Request for Comment" headings in the body (24 standalone in section II, plus "General Request for Comment", plus section-level E./G./G. headings in the economic analysis, PRA and RFA sections) — 31 including three table-of-contents lines. The second clause of F70 IS confirmed: questions run consecutively to 154, and Q154 asks for comments, views, estimates and data on market size, overall economic impact and other aspects of the economic analysis (lines 10703-10712). Drop the block count; keep 154.

unsupported.fact: F12 basis: "the RSS only gives title, author and time" (with an empty verbatim_quote).
unsupported.why: MISDESCRIBED. I re-fetched statements.rss (200, 25 items). <dc:creator> is empty in all three items; the name and role come from the <description> element ("Paul S. Atkins, Chairman", "Commissioner Hester M. Peirce", "Commissioner Mark T. Uyeda") and the URL slug from <link>. All three titles and all three timestamps (14:30:23, 14:30:21, 14:29:22 -0400 on Tue, 18 Aug 2026) are EXACTLY as recorded and the roles ARE supported — but by a field the researcher did not name, and the fact carries no quote at all. Re-state the basis before using it.

unsupported.fact: F03: "91 FR 54510, Volume 91, Issue 161 (Friday, 21 August 2026), pages 54510-54655, 146 pages" attributed to the Federal Register API JSON.
unsupported.why: TRACEABILITY MISMATCH (content is right). The API gives citation "91 FR 54510", start_page 54510, end_page 54655, page_length 146 — all confirmed — but carries NO issue number. "No. 161" and "Friday, August 21, 2026" come from the .txt/PDF header line, a different URL. Re-attach the issue-number half of this fact to the .txt or the GovInfo PDF.

unsupported.fact: F64 — the 3,165 crypto projects and the 475 safe-harbor issuers derived from it, recorded as usable.
unsupported.why: COMPLIANCE-INCONSISTENT with the researcher's own reasoning. The release states 3,165 exactly once (line 10814) with no footnote and no stated provenance; the only place in the release counting crypto assets by launch year is Figure 1, built from CoinMarketCap data (fn 438, "Crypto Market Overview, CoinMarketCap … last visited June 6, 2025"). The researcher excluded the 9,746 figure precisely because it is CoinMarketCap listing data barred by crypto.md, then kept 3,165 and the 475 derived from it. Either both go or the exclusion rationale is wrong. I would drop both and say so in unverified_or_excluded. The 130/99/31 PRA counts and the 636/581/14/41 Reg D-A-CF counts are fine — those are SEC filing counts, not market data.

unsupported.fact: sources[] coverage: F12 (statements.rss), F62 (api/2026-05635.json) and F72 (the FR search API query URL) cite URLs that are not among the four sources[].
unsupported.why: Not disqualifying for the research record — I fetched all three and all returned 200 and are first-party — but the article's sources[] is capped at 4 and none of these three is in it. The writer must not put a URL in the article that is not in sources[], so any fact resting on those three needs a sources[] slot or must be dropped.

additional_findings: MISSED AND MATERIAL — footnote 122 (lines 1577-1581): the proposed 'crypto asset' definition is 'identical to the definition of ``Digital Asset'' in section (2)(6) of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act, Public Law 119-27, 139 Stat. 419 (July 18, 2025).' This is the honest first-party bridge between C4 and C6-C9, and it also means F17's crypto-asset definition fact is incomplete as recorded.

MISSED AND MATERIAL — footnote 114 (lines 1443-1453): 'permitted payment stablecoins received for the covered investment contracts being offered' count toward the aggregate offering price / offering limit; fees paid by the investor that reduce the consideration the issuer receives do NOT count toward the limit; fees the issuer pays out of proceeds are a use of proceeds and are not deducted.

MISSED AND MATERIAL — Rule 228.304 'testing the waters' (lines 12919-12935): before qualification an issuer may solicit interest orally or in writing, but 'No solicitation or acceptance of money or other consideration, nor of any commitment, binding or otherwise, from any person is permitted until qualification of the offering statement', and the communication must say so on its face. The single most reader-protective provision in the release, omitted entirely.

MISSED AND MATERIAL — Rule 228.306 Suspension of the exemption (lines 13124-13180): the Commission may at any time temporarily suspend an exemption on six grounds (including material misstatement in the offering statement or any Rule 305 report, or failure to cooperate with an investigation); notice and a right to request a hearing within 30 calendar days; the order becomes permanent on the 30th calendar day if no hearing is requested. Plus Rule 228.101(d): an insignificant deviation does not void the exemption, but the failure remains actionable by the Commission under Securities Act section 20 and does not preclude a Rule 306 proceeding. Both support 'exemption is not immunity' better than anything recorded.

MISSED — 'Project Crypto' (lines 641-718): Exec. Order 14178 of 2025-01-23 established the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets; the PWG Report (2025-07-30) recommended a fit-for-purpose section 5 exemption, a time-limited safe harbor and an airdrop safe harbor; on 2025-07-31 Chairman Paul S. Atkins announced 'Project Crypto' and directed staff 'to swiftly develop proposals to implement the [PWG's] recommendations', expressly naming 'initial coin offerings', 'airdrops' and network rewards. This is the proposal's direct lineage.

MISSED — the release's own summary of the 2026 Interpretation (lines 722-740): it classified crypto assets into five categories (digital commodities, digital collectibles, digital tools, stablecoins, digital securities) and the Commission's view is that digital securities are securities, stablecoins may or may not be depending on characteristics, and the other three are not themselves securities. The clean one-paragraph way to relate C4 to C3 without stealing C3's material.

MISSED — legal basis and authority: section VIII.B states the rules are proposed under Securities Act sections 3(b), 18, 19(a) and 28 and Exchange Act sections 3(b), 12, 13, 15, 23(a) and 36; the new Part 228 authority citation is 15 U.S.C. 77c, 77r(b)(3), 77s, 77z-3, 78c(b), 78w and 78mm.

MISSED — proposed 17 CFR 200.30-1(n)(1) delegates to the Director of the Division of Corporation Finance the authority to grant applications under Rule 228.104 'upon a showing of good cause that it is not necessary under the circumstances that an exemption … be denied', i.e. a bad-actor disqualification waiver route exists. F23/F24 record the disqualification but not the waiver.

MISSED — Rule 228.300(c)(3)(ii): 'At the market offerings' (offerings at other than a fixed price) are NOT permitted under the fundraising exemption. And Rule 228.307(b): an offering statement on file nine months without amendment and not qualified may be declared abandoned.

MISSED nuance on preemption (lines 6714-6736, a better cite than F51's rule text): the preemption reaches secondary-market transactions by any person other than an issuer, underwriter or dealer, INCLUDING covered investment contracts initially sold under a different federal exemption, and that secondary preemption 'would continue for the period during which the issuer continues to satisfy the disclosure and filing and/or periodic reporting requirements' — so it can lapse.

MISSED caveat on F66: footnote 439 says the 14 Regulation A issuers were identified by keyword matching in Form 1-A offering circulars and 'The securities that the issuers were offering and selling, therefore, were not necessarily covered investment contracts', and that issuers cannot offer covered investment contracts under Regulation A at all. Also the release is internally inconsistent on the window: the summary says 'for the period from 2016 to 2024' while the Reg D subsection says filings were analysed 'from 2009 through 2024' with 'the first offerings appearing in 2017'. Use the release's own '2016 to 2024' framing and do not present 581/636 as a clean census.

BETTER FIRST-PARTY LINK FOR READERS: the API's html_url field gives the canonical page https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/21/2026-17183/regulation-crypto-assets. It is blocked to us (200 + Request Access) but is the canonical citation. The GovInfo PDF, which I verified end to end (146 pages, page 1 = 54510, SUMMARY/DATES matching), is the right link to hand readers since we confirmed its contents. Keep both facts straight in sourcing_notes.

The candidate list entry for C4 lists ONLY the blocked html_url as its source. It should be corrected to the raw_text_url plus the GovInfo PDF — I independently confirm the researcher's proposed correction is right. I also confirm the researcher's other candidate-list corrections: sec.gov/news/*.rss works (25 live items each) while /rss/rules/proposed.xml and /rss/news/speeches.xml are 403, and regulations.gov is 403 so its comment count cannot be checked live.

Independently strengthened F62: I fetched the March record's DATES field, which reads 'Effective Date: March 23, 2026.' So the March interpretation genuinely IS in force (CFTC + SEC, type 'Rule', action 'Final rule; interpretation; guidance', 91 FR 13714, S7-2026-09) and the contrast with the August proposal is solid. Its full text is reachable at https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/03/23/2026-05635.txt if C3 needs it.

Independently reproduced F72: FR search API count=1; a separate query for all SEC documents published since 2026-08-22 (count 171) returns nothing with 'crypto' in the title. As of 2026-09-16 there is no comment-period extension and no final rule.

On event_date I agree with the researcher's flag: all three dates are first-party sourced (approved 2026-08-18 per 'By the Commission. Dated: August 18, 2026.'; filed 2026-08-20 08:45; published 2026-08-21). BRIEF.md says the slug date is the event date, not the publication date, citing batch 3's rename of 20260709 to 20260708. Under that rule the slug should be …-20260818. Editorial call, not a fact error, but decide it before the writer starts and consistently with C3.

Overall: this is a much cleaner research record than the batch-3 baseline. 67 of 73 recorded facts are verbatim-accurate against the source, no fabricated URL or identifier, no news-outlet or aggregator sourcing, and the date separation and the 'proposal, not final rule' framing are correct and well guarded. The defects are concentrated in not_said (GENIUS Act, stablecoin characterisation) and editorial_brief (source-code publication), both of which would put false statements into the finished article, so they must be fixed before drafting.
